/look_brief.audience: a private equity sponsor's investment committee (partners, the deal team, the fund's credit and portfolio-operations heads) who test every assumption, recompute the returns and look for where the case breaks
/look_brief.occasion: six pages of the leveraged finance and LBO section of an investment committee book on Corvane Flow Systems, a fictional maker of engineered valves, pumps and aftermarket services; printed on US letter, read line by line at a desk with a pen the evening before the vote, never projected
/look_brief.subject_world: an industrial company lives on engineering drawings, bills of materials and test certificates: ruled grids, one value per cell, a title block that says which sheet of how many, dimension lines that state the size of a gap, and safety orange that marks a limit on the shop floor. The pages borrow the conventions that have a job here: sheet numbering in the footer ('Sheet n'), dimension-style brackets that state the size of a headroom or a value bridge step, BOM-like ruled tables with heavy rules at head and foot, and a dark orange kept for limits (the covenant, the hurdle). They leave out drawing borders, grid references, a monospaced drawing face (it fits fewer digits per column), gear or valve icons, blueprint blue grounds and photographs of plant, which would be costume with no job and would cost the space the figures need
/look_brief.data_character: a full LBO case: six years of history by three segments, a 34-line five-year operating model with debt schedule, sources and uses, a four-tranche capital structure, three return sensitivity grids of up to 5 by 7 cells, a 12-deal financing comps table and a 12-company trading comps table with mean, median, high and low rows, a base and a downside leverage path against a covenant, and four exit routes. Four to six exhibits a page, most of them tables; charts only where the reader must see a shape (leverage against the covenant, the value bridge, end-market mix, MOIC by exit route)

density.target: extremely dense, a senior associate's IC book: four to six exhibits a page, tables of 12 to 34 rows and 8 to 11 columns at the 7pt floor, 400 to 700 words a page, every exhibit with a units line, footnotes and a source line, 0.15in gutters
density.why: the committee reads every line before it votes and wants the operating case, the debt it supports and the returns it earns on facing pages without turning; each table a member checks (sources and uses, the model, the grids, the comps) must be whole on one page, and the comps carry their statistics rows because the exit multiple is argued from them

/look_brief.look: engineering-plain: white letter pages, Carlito throughout, a deep steel blue for Corvane and the base case, safety orange only for limits, grey for peers and history, red only for a case that misses a limit; ruled like a bill of materials, topic titles over one blue rule, sheet-numbered footers, nothing decorative

colour_meanings.color.accent1: Corvane's own figures and the base case: the subject row, the base-case series and cell, the projected years' structure, the title rule
colour_meanings.color.accent4: Corvane's second series where one is not enough: the junior tranche in the capital stack, the prior history behind the forecast in a chart
colour_meanings.color.accent2: a limit and nothing else: the springing covenant maximum, the 20% IRR and 2.5x MOIC hurdles, written as a line or the threshold column
colour_meanings.color.accent3: peers, precedents and context: comps bars, history in a chart, the equity layer as the residual
colour_meanings.color.negative: a case or cell that misses a limit: an IRR under the hurdle, the downside leverage path, a headroom under 30%
colour_meanings.color.surface_alt: a block head inside a table and the base-case cell of a grid, as a BOM groups its assemblies

/look_brief.type_ladder: built down from the densest page, the five-year operating model: 34 lines by 9 year columns plus a label column must sit beside an assumptions table on a 10.2in measure, which fits at 7pt cells with 0.02in padding and no larger, so table text, footnotes, source lines, units lines and chart text all sit at the 7pt floor, measured for Calibri, whose metrics Carlito matches; the committee reads the notes in 8pt body, exhibit heads step up to 9pt bold blue, KPI figures to 14pt, and a 15pt topic title stays on one line. Five sizes in all (15, 14, 9, 8, 7)

rejected.what: claim titles that argue the deal
rejected.why: an IC book titles each page by topic and states the view in the notes column and the takeaways; the committee forms its own view from the figures

rejected.what: filled header rows on every table
rejected.why: on pages carrying five tables a filled header is the loudest thing on the page six times over; a heavy rule under the heads separates them

rejected.what: zebra banding on every other row
rejected.why: at 7pt on a 34-line table banding reads as stripes and fights the block heads, which carry the grouping the reader needs

rejected.what: green for good and red for bad on the sensitivity grids
rejected.why: a heat map gives colour a meaning per cell; the grids mark only what misses the hurdle in red and box the base case, so colour keeps one meaning

rejected.what: a monospaced engineering face for figures
rejected.why: it fits about a fifth fewer digits per column at the same size and the 11-column tables would not fit
no job on a page that is read for its figures, and none would survive at the space they would take
every bar and point carries its value; the only horizontal line on a chart is a limit

/reference/page.why: US letter landscape, 11 x 8.5 in: the book is printed and read at a desk

/typography/roles/type.title.why: a topic title on one line, the largest text on the page and still modest beside dense tables

/typography/roles/type.kicker.why: the section tag above the title in Corvane blue, at the floor

/typography/roles/type.kpi.why: the headline figures of the overview strip, one step under the title

/typography/roles/type.h1.why: an exhibit head, one step over the notes, in the structure colour

/typography/roles/type.h2.why: a run-in head at body size in the notes column

/typography/roles/type.body.why: notes read at a desk, one step over the 7pt tables

/typography/roles/type.emphasis.why: the bold run inside a note

/typography/roles/type.caption.why: the units line under an exhibit head, italic so it reads as a qualifier

/typography/roles/type.footnote.why: definitions and assumptions under an exhibit, at the floor

/typography/roles/type.source_line.why: one source line per page above the footer

/typography/roles/type.table_header.why: bold column heads over a heavy rule, at the cell size

/typography/roles/type.table_cell.why: the densest text in the book: the 34-line model fits at 7pt

/typography/roles/type.axis_label.why: chart axis text, quieter than the values

/typography/roles/type.data_label.why: values on the marks, bold so the figure reads before the bar

/color/roles/color.surface_alt.why: a pale steel for block heads and the base-case cell, light enough that 7pt ink reads on it

/color/roles/color.ink_muted.why: secondary text, above 4.5:1 on white and on the block heads

/color/roles/color.accent1.why: a deep steel blue for Corvane and the base case

/extra_roles/color.accent4.why: a lighter steel for Corvane's second series

/color/roles/color.accent2.why: safety orange darkened until it reads as 7pt text: limits only

/color/roles/color.accent3.why: a grey for peers, history and context that recedes

/color/roles/color.negative.why: red for a case or cell that misses a limit

/extra_roles/color.ink_inverse.why: values set inside the blue bars and stack segments

/chrome.why: a blue rule closes the title zone, the one structural line every sheet shares
a hairline sets off the title block at the foot of the sheet

/chrome.text: Project Corvane  |  Investment committee book  |  Section 4: Leveraged finance and LBO  |  Strictly confidential  |  Illustrative figures, fictional company
/chrome.why: a printed sheet says whose book it is, which section, and that its figures are illustrative
the drawing title block's sheet number: the committee refers to pages by sheet

/tables.why: ruled like a bill of materials: a heavy rule under the heads and at the foot, hairlines between lines, no fills but block heads and the base case

/charts.why: labelled marks in Corvane blue, peers in grey, one orange limit line, no gridlines

/description.summary: Engineering-plain and ruled like a bill of materials: white letter sheets, Carlito at the 7pt floor, deep steel blue for Corvane and the base case, safety orange only for limits.
/description.typography: Carlito throughout on a 15, 14, 9, 8, 7pt ladder built down to the 7pt model table.
/description.color: Blue is Corvane and the base case, light steel its second series, orange a limit, grey peers and history, red a case that misses a limit; nothing else is coloured.
/description.layout: 0.4in margins, a topic title over a blue rule, four to six exhibits per sheet on 0.15in gutters, a notes column where the page argues, a sheet-numbered footer.
/description.tables: No header fill, a heavy ink rule under the heads and at the foot, hairlines between lines, pale steel block heads, the base case boxed.
/description.motifs: the blue title rule; dimension brackets stating a gap; sheet numbers

/continuation.why: a split table repeats its title with (continued) and its heads; none is split in this section
